storage.parser_metadata: state, reserved bit, input_seen, event8, status8, snapshot1

lifetime: Existing full command ticket/job owner is retained from native acceptance through real terminal take.
INPUT event3 matches session/record and full metadata. It ACKs only at actual EOP with recipient ready and does not complete range or free command/result storage.
RF event4 SOP matches the existing command. A snapshot reserves the existing result_tail before any payload is accepted; partial assembly counts against the same two result slots.
RF metadata must match context/n/group/nextK/fullK/ticket/Wbank/generation/use. Unknown or malformed frames drain without completing the command.
FINAL/SPILL low/high 128-bit words write directly into the reserved FIFO entry. High-word EOP capture and publication are one atomic edge.
CONTINUE has no result payload or S write; it still completes the record only after exact RF metadata and EOP.
Snapshot terminal requires two distinct actual S128 write ACKs. INPUT consumed and snapshot stored are independent events.

Matching ABORT event5 uses original EXEC session/record and four flits. Context/actual-nextK range and alignment, full input key and independent RFowner are checked in place. It does not become a snapshot or a range continuation at partial K16 prefix.

The guard exposes held native_abort_valid/ticket/nextK only after exact ABORT EOP. It retains the command until that observation is accepted and matching cancel_drained arrives. Withholding real A/W/DMA drain keeps the owner live.

Other native control frames pass straight to the bounded native scheduler; this parser does not validate their event-specific body or free an owner on them. In particular, unowned transport FAULT is not implicitly attributed to the active command.

cancel_drained_valid still requires production integration with A/raw flush, held transport and all actual DMA returns. The guard now independently requires the actual verified ABORT, but the remaining source-drain coordinator is not established by the unit fixture.
